movingBand.observation: Not blind: historical moving media and the 3,000-tick prefix were already available. From 5,500 to 6,000, the middle-left occupied group expands upward and rightward into a much broader branching cluster. The lower-left groups clear and reform as a narrower descending chain nearer the center, with a new broad group at the bottom-center edge. These are occupied-shape changes, not color or food-outline changes.

stationaryBand.observation: The dense upper-middle cluster at 5,500 largely clears, leaving a thin upper chain and a wider gap below it. A broad branching group develops along the middle-left edge. The large lower-middle/right groups clear into separated small groups, opening a broad lower gap by 6,000.

sameAgeComparisons.observation: Moving groups occupy mainly the right half; stationary groups are mostly on the left, with isolated lower-middle branches. This is the exact historical prefix.
Moving has a middle-left cluster and scattered upper/lower groups; stationary has a dense upper-middle cluster and separate lower-middle groups.
Moving has a broad upper-middle branching cluster and descending lower chain; stationary has a middle-left cluster and widely separated groups. This difference is descriptive, not an advantage gate.
